proposal: The Mandate recommends rules to give Clean Water Act section 308 a clear and enforced time limit, to clarify the criminal negligence standard under sections 402 and 404, to prohibit retroactive or preemptive section 404 permits, to promote nutrient trading using a carrot rather than stick approach, and to update compensatory mitigation without imposing new requirements beyond current law (p. 429). The waters of the United States and section 401 items are tracked separately.

status_summary: On 2026-01-08 the Army Corps of Engineers published the reissuance of its nationwide permits under section 404, effective 2026-03-15, retaining the 2021 compensatory mitigation thresholds. On 2026-03-13 Executive Order 14394 directed the Army and EPA to review and revise federal standards for section 404 permits and for state and tribal assumption of 404 programs, among other water requirements affecting housing, without a deadline. No rule on section 308 time limits, criminal negligence, retroactive or preemptive permits, nutrient trading or compensatory mitigation was found.

timeline.event: The Army Corps of Engineers published its final reissuance and modification of the nationwide permits, effective 2026-03-15 and expiring 2031-03-15, retaining the 2021 compensatory mitigation thresholds (91 FR 768 to 886, docket COE-2025-0002; 56 existing permits reissued and one new permit issued).

Executive Order 14394, Removing Regulatory Barriers to Affordable Home Construction, was signed; section 2(a) directs the Army and EPA to review and revise section 404 permit standards and standards for state assumption of 404 programs (published 2026-03-18, 91 FR 13207).

title: Reform Clean Water Act 308, 404, nutrient trading and compensatory mitigation rules
uncertainties: Absence of evidence rests on Federal Register API queries (compensatory mitigation, water quality trading, nationwide permits under the Army Department listing, which returned none) and one web search; the nationwide permit rule was read only in part (a fetch of the govinfo PDF). Nationwide permits were reissued on the Corps' regular five-year cycle and are not what the Mandate asked for, so the match is parallel. Waters of the United States proposals (2025-11-20 and 2026-09-09) are tracked in c13-06 and are not counted here. Whether EPA has opened a docket or notice for the section 308 or trading items was not found. In this pass, Federal Register API searches for compensatory mitigation (from 2026-03-01), water quality trading and section 308 information requests (from 2025-01-20) returned no document on any listed item; the searches matched loosely and returned many unrelated documents. Executive Order 14394 section 2(a) was read and does not mention section 308, nutrient trading or mitigation, and sets no deadline. The nationwide permit final action was read as Federal Register metadata and abstract, not its full 119 pages, so the mitigation threshold statement rests on the earlier review.
